items.title: LDC : Jackson en feu, Assane Diao buteur et blessé
items.description: Ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026, plusieurs internationaux sénégalais ont marqué la soirée européenne, pour le meilleur comme pour le pire. Nicolas Jackson a inscrit un doublé dans la large victoire 6-0 d'Aston Villa contre Fenerbahçe. L'attaquant sénégalais a été décisif et a lancé son équipe vers un succès sans appel. Ibrahim Mbaye a lui aussi brillé en délivrant une passe décisive en 2e période. Assane Diao a également trouvé le chemin des filets avant de quitter ses partenaires sur blessure, lors de la défaite de Côme 2-3 sur la pelouse de Feyenoord. L’ailier a ouvert le score dès la 18e minute, avant de sortir, touché, dans la foulée. La nature de la blessure n'a pas été précisée, et son état sera à surveiller dans les prochains jours. Iliman Ndiaye passeur à Manchester Iliman Ndiaye a délivré une passe décisive, mais cela n'a pas suffi : Manchester City s'est incliné face à Paris 2-4, à domicile. Entre l'efficacité de Jackson, le but de Diao et la passe décisive de Mbaye, la soirée a offert de belles satisfactions aux supporters des Lions. Reste l'inquiétude autour d'Assane Diao, dont le staff sénégalais attendra des nouvelles. O.B.N

items.title: Potentiel économique, port de Ndayane, opportunités de partenariat: les géants du maritime font cap sur Dakar
items.description: Avec 700 km de côte et le port de Ndayane en chantier, Dakar attire les géants du commerce maritime. Ils peaufinent leurs stratégies à travers le renforcement de leurs moyens logistiques et le lancement de nouveaux projets. L’objectif est de mieux se positionner sur le marché. Le Sénégal est à la croisée des grandes routes maritimes grâce à un potentiel certain en matière de commerce international. Le pays dispose de 700 km de côtes et du port de Dakar, doté d’une position stratégique. Non loin de là, émerge le futur port de Ndayane. Autant de facteurs qui repositionnent le pays sur l’échiquier mondial, aiguisant l'appétit des grands groupes. Parmi eux figure Msc (Mediterranean shipping company), référence du transport de conteneurs. Son président, Diego Aponte, a été reçu, le 8 octobre 2026, à Dakar, par le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Les échanges ont porté sur le renforcement des infrastructures portuaires et logistiques du Sénégal, le développement de son potentiel maritime et son intégration aux grandes routes du commerce mondial. Ainsi, le groupe Msc a exprimé sa volonté de renforcer sa présence au Sénégal et de proposer des solutions adaptées aux besoins du pays. Diego Aponte a également réaffirmé la disponibilité du groupe à accompagner la mise en œuvre de l’Agenda national de transformation « Sénégal 2050 ». Avant Msc, un autre géant, Cma Cgm, avait manifesté son intérêt pour renforcer ses positions à Dakar. Lors d’une audience avec le chef de l’État à l’occasion de l’Africa Forward, à Nairobi, Rodolphe Saadé a affirmé sa volonté d’accompagner le Sénégal dans sa nouvelle trajectoire de développement. Les secteurs visés sont particulièrement le port de Ndayane et les Zones économiques spéciales (Zes), devenues une politique phare de l’État. Avec une flotte d’environ 700 porte-conteneurs et une présence dans plus de 170 pays, Cma Cgm entend mettre en place des infrastructures structurantes appelées à repositionner le Sénégal comme un hub logistique majeur sur la façade atlantique et à générer durablement de l'activité, des emplois et des recettes pour l’économie nationale. Au moment où d’autres sont en approche, Maersk œuvre à renforcer sa présence. Il y a quelques mois, la compagnie s’est implantée à Dalifort avec l’un des plus grands entrepôts d’exploitation. Bâti sur une superficie de 5.100 m2, ce site, entièrement optimisé par un système de gestion digital avancé, vise à renforcer la capacité d’entreposage et de distribution dans la région ouest-africaine en répondant aux standards internationaux les plus exigeants, selon Thomas Theeuwes, directeur régional de Maersk pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest. Hub portuaire Présent depuis longtemps à Dakar et impliqué dans de grands projets, tels que le port de Ndayane, Dp World (Dubaï port world) est également dans une logique de renforcement de son assise au Sénégal. Dans son rapport d’activités, la compagnie met en avant des ambitions comme la création d’emplois directs et indirects, la contribution significative au Produit intérieur brut (Pib), la dynamisation des chaînes de valeur locales et le renforcement de la compétitivité du Sénégal sur les corridors commerciaux régionaux et internationaux. Parallèlement, une étude sur l’impact socioéconomique des activités de Dp World au Sénégal révèle que la société émiratie a contribué, en moyenne, à hauteur de 555 milliards de FCfa au Pib du pays et à des recettes fiscales estimées à plus de 112 milliards de FCfa entre 2022 et 2024, sans compter près de 170.000 emplois créés. Ces intérêts se manifestent dans un contexte où le Sénégal entend s’établir en véritable hub logistique. « Nous voulons faire du Sénégal une plateforme maritime de référence. Inscrite dans l’Agenda national de Transformation « Sénégal 2050 », cette ambition repose sur plusieurs axes prioritaires : la modernisation des infrastructures portuaires, le développement des corridors logistiques, la promotion d’un transport maritime durable, la sécurisation des espaces maritimes, la formation des ressources humaines et la préservation des écosystèmes », a déclaré le président Faye lors du Forum international sur le développement durable des transports maritimes dans l'économie bleue tenu en juillet 2026. Demba DIENG

items.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle Broke Trump’s Most Important Rule
items.description: After half-heartedly including some actual professionals in his first administration, Donald Trump is now served almost exclusively by sycophants and family members. The president has made clear that he cares about loyalty more than qualifications, but the astonishing incompetence and corruption of many of his appointees raises an obvious question: What does it take to get fired by Trump’s White House? Kimberly Guilfoyle’s resignation yesterday as ambassador to Greece provides some clues. Guilfoyle has been accused of blatant corruption both before and during her time as an envoy. She denies these allegations, but her resignation—which the White House requested—isn’t really about corruption. The idea that Guilfoyle, and only Guilfoyle, crossed some sort of previously unseen corruption red line is laughable. If ethical and legal questions, including the now-moribund standard of “appearances of impropriety,” were grounds for dismissal in this administration, Trump would have already shed several other members of his team. Rather, Guilfoyle was pushed out because she was an embarrassment. She overstepped her bounds, tried to trade on the president’s name, and then made the administration look bad when she got caught. Also, she is a woman, and in this administration, self-dealing is mostly a man’s game. Indeed, by comparison with the charges leveled at others—including against the president himself, who seems utterly unconcerned with notions such as “emoluments”—Guilfoyle is decidedly a small-timer. This past spring, for example, the Financial Times reported that a broker for Pete Hegseth attempted to make a big investment in defense industries just before the Iran war, raising suspicions of insider trading . FBI Director Kash Patel has been accused of using government money as a slush fund to pay improper bonuses to his favorites within the Bureau. “Border Czar” Tom Homan was caught on audio in 2024 accepting $50,000 in cash (wrapped in a Cava food bag , always the sign of a deal on the up-and-up) from undercover FBI agents posing as business executives, and yet he remains in his job. Hegseth and Homan deny any wrongdoing; Patel and the FBI have offered no comment or explanation. And the journalist Dexter Filkins recently described Trump’s son-in-law and roving minister-without-portfolio Jared Kushner as representative of “a new kind of Washington figure, for whom public office serves as a means to extraordinary wealth.” [ Read: Trump’s team of mercenaries ] Guilfoyle may have been a relative piker among giants in the grift game, but her real sin was the pathetic and humiliating nature of her behavior. (Even Homan managed not to seem quite so grubby when reportedly accepting a bag of greenbacks.) Her messages to a Trump donor asking for money to help pay her huge credit-card bills are cringe-inducing. “Honey please I need you to get this done for me today,” she wrote to the Trump supporter Eric Deters when asking him to wire a cool $100,000 directly into her American Express account in July 2025, just before her confirmation hearings. Worse, she continually told Deters to stop writing things down and just contact her on Signal. “What a nightmare you’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing,” she said. This was apparently Guilfoyle’s version of the infamous “Stringer Bell rule,” named for a character from the television series The Wire who dressed down one of his drug-dealing accomplices for being stupid enough to keep written notes on a criminal conspiracy. The problem is that she, too, violated that rule: She made her requests to Deters to stop writing things down in writing . Deters, unsurprisingly, kept all the messages. Guilfoyle, he asserts, offered him access to the Trump administration. “I will be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever,” he claims she told him. When she didn’t deliver, he warned Guilfoyle and White House officials earlier this month that he would go public with their correspondence and then made good on that threat. The newly minted ambassador, meanwhile, was flitting about southeastern Europe in the company of Greek tycoons. But again, rather than enjoy the perks of her job in discreet luxury, she bragged about her connections to these wealthy men and tried to present herself as some sort of made woman from the inner Trump orbit who had the juice to get things done. According to The Wall Street Journal , she went to Davos in January 2026 and was excluded from a dinner being held for Eric Trump. She decided to pressure an American businessman to help her get in. “You know, I can deliver the world to you. Which you deserve,” she said. (This time, she was caught on audio , rather than by text message.) “I’m going to make you a lot of fucking money,” she told the American. She also raged about the impudence of the dinner’s Greek hostess. “You don’t have the fucking U.S., you know, ambassador to Greece not come. She should be kissing my fucking ass.” Again, Trump Sr. has no problem with F-bombs; he deploys them regularly. He has no problem with money grabs while in public office; he has enriched himself while president and has explicitly or implicitly blessed similar efforts by other subordinates to profit from their positions. But he apparently draws a line when his son’s former fiancée does not show proper appreciation for the courtesy of being stashed in Athens— Athens!— and then lands in the newspapers looking like an aging waitress cadging tips from marks in a casino. Honey, just put it on the tray. Don’t tell my manager, and I’ll get you to the good poker table. [ David Frum: Trump’s last loyal constituency ] Guilfoyle was once so tight with the Trumps that she was given a prime-time slot to fawn over the president during the 2020 GOP convention. It was a disastrous, over-the-top performance, but Trump loved it, reportedly calling her “my Kimberly” and comparing her to the former Argentine first lady Eva Perón. Earlier this year, Trump said of his emissary to Greece: “Kimberly Guilfoyle has been my friend for a long time. I love calling her Kimber-lay. That’s my little pet name, right? But you are the greatest, and I heard they love you over there.” But over the past several days, the president saw bad publicity about this demanding, middle-aged woman, thrown over by his son for a younger wife—as Trump himself has done to previous spouses—trying to profit off his presidency while making a fool of herself and encouraging more bad press about corruption just before the midterm elections. Guilfoyle had to go, and Trump jettisoned her quickly and coldly. “She wasn’t a member of my family,” the president said yesterday. “She, uh, I guess dated my son a long time ago.” “Dated”? I guess ? She was in line for years to become the president’s daughter-in-law, married to his first-born son. Now she’s just some dame one of his kids used to know. Guilfoyle didn’t get it. All she had to do was stay out of trouble. But that was too hard for her, and now she’s learned that making money off this presidency means following some rules. Don’t be too obvious; don’t embarrass the boss; don’t get caught if you can help it. And especially, don’t be an older woman .

items.title: Tebboune annonce la fabrication d’une voiture algérienne en 2028
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune , a rencontré les chefs d’entreprises ce mercredi 14 octobre au CIC d’Alger. Durant cette rencontre, la troisième du genre en trois ans, le chef de l’État a évoqué la fabrication d’une voiture algérienne à l’horizon 2028. « Si les choses se déroulent comme nous les avons planifiées avec les Allemands et les Italiens, nous aurons une voiture algérienne d’ici la fin 2028, avec une boîte de vitesses algérienne et des pneumatiques algériens, et pas seulement du gonflage de pneus. C’est un pari que nous tiendrons », a affirmé le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Tebboune sur la voiture algérienne : « C’est un pari que nous tiendrons » L’Algérie a lancé un vaste chantier pour se doter d’une véritable industrie automobile capable de fabriquer des véhicules avec un taux d’intégration de 30 %. Ce chantier a été lancé en 2023 avec l’installation de la marque Fiat du groupe Stellantis, qui a ouvert une usine à Oran, où elle fabrique le modèle Doblo tôlé et panoramique. Depuis septembre 2025, Fiat Algérie a lancé la fabrication de la Grande Panda en mode CKD, une première pour l’industrie automobile algérienne. Cette voiture, qui n’est pas encore sortie des chaînes, devrait atteindre un taux d’intégration de 30 %. D’autres constructeurs automobiles de taille mondiale comme Hyundai et Chery ont annoncé des projets de fabrication de voitures en Algérie. Entre-temps, l’Algérie a lancé des usines de fabrication de composants plastiques, de plaquettes de frein et de carrosseries pour véhicules. items.title: 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu
items.description: Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, for 2027, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to go home and let Nigeria breathe. Adebayo said this in a statement, in Abuja, on Wednesday. He was responding to the President’s plan to excuse himself from the rigors of physical campaigns in some states ahead of the presidential polls. Tinubu spoke at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continues to attend to matters of governance. In response, Adebayo said if Tinubu is too tired to campaign, he is too weak to govern. In a statement signed by his Presidential Campaign’s Chief Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, the SDP candidate described Tinubu as a “president in absentia” at a time Nigeria needs hands-on leadership. Adebayo said, “Nigeria is too complex, too dynamic, and currently too distressed to be governed by remote control.” He cited what he called repeated instances of the President governing from a distance, including prolonged medical vacations disguised as working visits, absence during national emergencies and reliance on proxies to announce state policies. The SDP candidate further said, “We have seen repeated instances where the President is visibly missing when the country needs reassurance. “From unannounced foreign trips during critical economic decisions to his complete silence during widespread regional protests, he has consistently acted like a president in absentia. If you are too tired to campaign, you are too weak to govern.” Adebayo alleged that the decision to stay off the campaign trail was not about strategy but fear. “The excuse of bowing out of the 2027 campaign is a cowardly smokescreen. The truth is that the President is terrified of the Nigerian people,” he argued. According to him, the administration’s economic policies – fuel subsidy removal fallout, skyrocketing inflation and currency instability -have made the President unpopular. “He knows the pain his bad policies have inflicted on families. He is hiding because he cannot face public anger, and he knows any appearance on a campaign trail will be met with collective booing of a betrayed populace.” Adebayo also said, “It is time to face reality: step aside, go home, and let this country breathe.” He called on the administration to prioritise national interest over political survival and be transparent about the President’s capacity to lead for the remainder of his term. The post 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigerians better off under Tinubu, APC spokesman insists
items.description: By Dickson Omobola National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Felix Muoka, has insisted that Nigeria and Nigerians are better off than ever before, saying the party will win the 2027 presidential election based on its positive records. Muoka said the APC was working hard to secure voters’ support, adding that the party would not take Nigerians’ votes for granted. Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Thursday, he said the party’s preparations and campaign efforts were aimed at securing as many votes as possible in the next general elections. He said: “Qualitatively speaking, our country is better. Nigerians are better today than they have ever been. Is there a country that has transited from this depressed economy, like we have had for decades, to that level of prosperity that didn’t go through these stages? “Nigerians also understand that. So what the president has done is to give this country a fighting chance, not just at recovery, but at building the prospects for sustainable prosperity.” On the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, he said: “What you saw today and what we’ve been up to is really taking ourselves seriously. If we thought this was all said and done, we wouldn’t put in this level of energy and work in an effort to really get to the last vote within the electorate. We are not taking this for granted. We’re taking it very seriously. I’m sure that if our party was docile and we were doing nothing to campaign or put out our information, you would also bring me here to say that we had been very docile. We’re a political party. “We are a party for a reason. We are in this to compete with other political parties and to win the support of Nigerians. Since 2023, there’s a reason that our party has been very successful. Since the last general elections, we’ve won fantastically all elections in which we have contested. There’s a reason for that. It’s because we prepare. We do our homework. “Nigerians bought in and voted for our party massively in 2023. We won that election, even though there are elements who want to claim that they won without evidence. But we won that election without question. As I said a few minutes ago, in every other election that has been called since then, Nigerians voted, not Indians. Nigerians voted in all the other elections since 2023. We won by upwards of 90 per cent. “Let me remind you that the APC is the governing party in this country, put in office by Nigerians. Already, the answer to your question has been codified in an election in which the APC is governing, not just at the centre, but in so many states in our country.” On the APC’s chances in 2027, he said: “We will win the election. We are working hard to win the election. I think that Nigerians are going to stand tall, shoulder to shoulder with the APC to win the next election.” Vanguard News The post Nigerians better off under Tinubu, APC spokesman insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG fixes August 2027 deadline for WAEC, NECO results
items.description: By Joseph Erunke The Federal Government has proposed a new examination timetable that will see candidates sitting the 2027 West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO) and other major external examinations receive their results by August, ahead of the September admission process into tertiary institutions. Under the proposed schedule, the government is seeking to end delays in the release of examination results that could disrupt candidates’ transition from secondary schools to universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. A statement on Wednesday night by the Director, Press and Public Relations of the Federal Ministry of Education, Boriowo Folasade, said the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, disclosed the plan during a meeting with heads and representatives of examination bodies at the Federal Ministry of Education headquarters in Abuja. “The meeting focused on harmonising examination schedules, preventing clashes among major examinations and ensuring that results are processed and released within agreed timelines, “the statement said. According to the proposed timetable, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) will conduct the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) from March 15 to 25, with results expected in the same month. NECO’s Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) is scheduled to hold from April 1 to May 14, while WAEC’s West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) will run from May 11 to June 18. Both NECO and WAEC are expected to release their results in August 2027. The National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) examination is proposed for June 1 to July 5, while the National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies (NBAIS) examination will hold from June 10 to July 9. Results from both examinations are also expected in August. The proposed schedule places the examination bodies under pressure to complete their respective processes in time to meet the government’s August results-release target. The Federal Ministry of Education said the initiative was part of the education reform agenda of the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, under the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), which seeks to improve efficiency, coordination and educational outcomes. It added that engagement with examination bodies would continue to ensure compliance with the proposed timelines, strengthen accountability and align the release of results with tertiary admission schedules. The government, under President Bola Tinubu, said it remained committed to reforms that would improve the efficiency of the education system and expand timely access to tertiary education. However, the timetable remains proposed, with the success of the plan depending on effective coordination among the examination bodies and their ability to meet the agreed deadlines. If implemented as planned, the initiative could give candidates and their parents greater certainty over the transition from secondary school examinations to tertiary admissions, while reducing disruptions caused by late results. Vanguard News The post FG fixes August 2027 deadline for WAEC, NECO results appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Achakzai sees governor's rule next being imposed in Sindh, over water and mines
items.description: Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai warned on Wednesday that governor’s rule would be imposed next in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”, urging the Centre to give provinces their rights and resources. He was speaking in the National Assembly, where a resolution endorsing the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday was passed . The federal government cited the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism as the reason for imposing governor’s rule in KP. In days preceding the development, political tensions between the federal government and the opposition, mainly the PTI, had remained high after the party announced a long march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. However, the march, initially planned for Islamabad, remained confined to KP until it fizzled out with the imposition of governor’s rule in the province. In his address, Achakzai said KP’s “mistake is that it saved itself with the help of its people”. He also drew a comparison between the current situation with regards to KP and the one witnessed at the time of the creation of Bangladesh. He also assailed the government for depriving the PTI of its election symbol ahead of the 2024 general elections. “And the mistake of his (Imran’s) party’s workers was that they contested the elections on 200 different symbols and turned your own game around on you. You are meting out the punishment for that? You are punishing 240 million people of Pakistan for that?” The opposition leader also pointed out that Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the chief minister after the imposition of governor’s rule and had been leading the PTI’s march, had not resorted to violence or using expletives in his call for the protest. He went on to say, “When you try to snatch our right to self-determination, our right to vote, we all will stand against you. All of us, all provinces.” Noting the participation of the PPP, which is in power in Sindh, Achakzai said it pained him. He then warned that governor’s rule would next be imposed in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”. “And then you will recall your mistake,” he said, noting however that there was still time to rectify mistakes. “Reverse these decisions,” Achakzai said, urging that Parliament be made the centre of power. “And Pakistan will be saved.” He warned that when the “state turns against its own people, they are compelled to look elsewhere”. The opposition also criticised the government over the country’s economic situation. “You are looting this country’s resources […] Have some mercy on this country. […] This country is drowning because of our mistakes. There is only one way to save it: through its Constitution and Parliament and by having a democratic system,” he asserted. Achakzai also lamented the fact the Parliament was not taken into confidence over decisions related to foreign affairs, and that Pakistan had strained ties with most of its neighbours. On Imran, who has not been allowed meetings with his family and associates for a long time, Achakzai said: “Which provision of the Constitution … places a restriction on meetings with the most popular leader of the country?” He assured that if meetings were arranged with Imran, “we will just try to assess his health condition and will try to resolve matter between you. We promise we will meet him and not tell anyone. […] Have some sense. Negotiate.” He concluded his address by declaring that the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP was wrong.

items.title: Tebboune face aux patrons : discours apaisé et bilan satisfaisant de l’économie algérienne
items.description: Troisième rencontre en trois ans du président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune , avec les opérateurs économiques, réunis ce mercredi 14 octobre au Centre international des conférences (CIC) d’Alger à l’initiative du Conseil du renouveau économique algérien (CREA). Dans un discours de 45 minutes, au ton apaisé, Abdelmadjid Tebboune a fait un état des lieux de l'économie algérienne , a exprimé son satisfecit de ce qui a été fait et a réitéré sa confiance aux chefs d'entreprise. Les difficultés qui subsistent sont dues au passage « qui n'est pas toujours facile » d’une économie dirigée à une économie de marché. Les pratiques néfastes qui continuent à être déplorées sont le fait de « la minorité des minorités ». Tebboune remonte le moral aux chefs d'entreprise Le président a fait le choix d’un discours apaisé pour booster le moral des patrons qui en ont plus que jamais besoin dans une conjoncture internationale difficile et au moment où la stratégie de relance et de diversification de l'économie est en « passe d'atteindre tous ses objectifs », à l’orée de « l’année pivot » 2027. Ceux qui s'attendaient à entendre la colère du président, à la suite de l'affaire des exagérations dans les demandes d’importation formulées par certains opérateurs, n'ont pas vu juste. L'affaire a été divulguée début septembre par le ministère du Commerce extérieur et avait provoqué une réunion au sommet présidée par le chef de l’État en personne. Des entreprises, employant parfois une ou deux personnes, ont introduit des demandes d’importation d’une valeur cumulée de 130 milliards de dollars. Tebboune appelle à combattre ensemble les « parasites » Dans son discours de ce mercredi, Tebboune a évidemment évoqué ce dépassement, sans toutefois trop s’y attarder et, surtout, sans en faire le reproche à toute la sphère économique. Au contraire, il a appelé les opérateurs à contribuer à débusquer et à lutter contre ces pratiques et leurs auteurs. « Le parasite qui n'a pas compris que l’Algérie a changé, nous devons le combattre ensemble », a-t-il dit. Ce ne sont pas, du reste, ces pratiques isolées qui peuvent ternir l'image des chefs d'entreprise, véritables « partenaires stratégiques de l’État », a reconnu le président qui a dénoncé les « tentatives d’épuiser les réserves de devises du pays ». Les chiffres de la transformation Pour le reste, les chiffres sont là pour plaider la bonne marche de l'économie nationale et de ses acteurs qui sont en passe de doter l’Algérie, « définitivement, d’une économie nouvelle et forte en 2027 ». Les importations ont été réduites « de manière structurelle » de 62 à 40-42 milliards de dollars grâce à l'apport de la production locale ; la production pharmaceutique couvre 84 % des besoins du pays contre à peine 10 % il n’y a pas longtemps ; l'industrie contribue désormais à 10 % du PIB après un long « désert industriel », la perspective d'avoir une « voiture algérienne » en 2028… En tout cas, « il y a une grande différence entre 2020 et aujourd'hui », et l'économie algérienne, qui était « désarticulée », est devenue « la troisième économie d’Afrique », et « pourquoi pas la première » à terme. L'Algérie enregistre aussi des taux de croissance appréciables, 3,8 % en 2025 et des prévisions à 4 % en 2026. Avant le chef de l'État, le ministre des Finances, Mohamed Lamine Lebbou, avait livré les chiffres du PIB brut, soit 36.103 milliards de dinars en 2024, 37.790 milliards en 2025 et un montant prévisionnel de plus de 42.000 milliards en 2026. M. Lebbou a expliqué que l’année 2011, prise comme année de référence pour le calcul du PIB, était « inadaptée » et qu'une autre année sera, de ce fait, choisie. « Passer en douceur, sans secousses » sociales Autre indicateur de la bonne marche vers l’édification d’une économie « résiliente face aux fluctuations de l'économie mondiale », Abdelmadjid Tebboune a cité le chiffre de 13.000 projets d’investissement concrets. Dans ce registre, le président a annoncé la concrétisation officielle du Guichet unique à partir du 1ᵉʳ janvier prochain. En attendant, Omar Rekkache, l'actuel directeur de l’AAPI, l'agence algérienne de promotion de l’investissement, sera maintenu pour mener la transition. Cette marche de l'Algérie vers une nouvelle économie ne se fera pas au détriment du citoyen et du volet social, s’est en outre engagé le président. Bien que « l’équation soit difficile », « nous essayons de passer en douceur, sans secousses », a-t-il indiqué, assurant que l’État ne se délestera pas de son caractère social. L’article Tebboune face aux patrons : discours apaisé et bilan satisfaisant de l’économie algérienne est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Éruption de Goumeri W-8 : le gouvernement nigérien intensifie la réponse technique et environnementale…
items.description: Les ministres du Pétrole, M. Hamadou Tini, et de l’Environnement, le colonel Abdoulaye Maizama, se sont rendus ce matin sur le bloc pétrolier d’Agadem pour évaluer, sur place, l’évolution de la situation au puits Goumeri W-8, touché depuis le 25 septembre 2026 par une éruption de pétrole brut et de gaz. La visite vise à superviser le déploiement des équipes techniques et l’application des mesures conservatoires destinées à sécuriser la plateforme dégradée, contenir le flux d’hydrocarbures et limiter les impacts environnementaux sur les sols et les ressources environnantes. Selon le ministère du Pétrole, la fuite est partiellement contenue, mais l’éruption se poursuit avec une intensité réduite. Les deux membres du gouvernement sont accompagnés d’une équipe d’experts algériens de la Sonatrach, arrivés expressément pour apporter leur expertise dans la maîtrise de l’incident. Leur mission porte notamment sur l’évaluation technique du puits, l’analyse des risques liés à l’éruption, le renforcement des dispositifs de sécurisation de la plateforme et l’appui à la conception des opérations de contrôle du flux. Cette collaboration s’inscrit dans le cadre de la coopération technique algéro-nigérienne dans les hydrocarbures, fondée sur le partage d’expertise, le transfert de savoir-faire, la formation et le renforcement des capacités du personnel nigérien. L’Algérie avait réaffirmé, avant l’incident, sa disponibilité à accompagner le Niger dans ce secteur à travers Sonatrach et ses filiales. Les experts algériens devraient également contribuer à l’enquête indépendante annoncée par le gouvernement afin de déterminer les causes de l’éruption et d’établir les responsabilités. Le ministre du Pétrole, M. Hamadou Tini, et son homologue de l’Environnement sont accompagnés du gouverneur de la région de Diffa, le général de division Ibrahim Bagadoma, des autorités locales et des équipes techniques mobilisées sur le site. La coordination vise à assurer une réponse simultanée sur les plans opérationnel, environnemental et sécuritaire. Le gouvernement a par ailleurs indiqué que des mesures conservatoires et de contrôle concernant l’opérateur ont été engagées, tandis que les opérations de sécurisation du site se poursuivent de jour comme de nuit. Source: Ministère du Pétrole du Niger L’article Éruption de Goumeri W-8 : le gouvernement nigérien intensifie la réponse technique et environnementale… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: 3 000 milliards de FCFA non rapatriés, nigérisation au point mort : L’État tape du poing sur la table face aux pétroliers chinois…
items.description: Cinq mois après la signature du protocole d’accord du 18 mai 2026, le gouvernement nigérien a dressé un bilan sans concession de la coopération pétrolière avec ses partenaires chinois. Dans un communiqué officiel, lu le 13 octobre 2026 par le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Bakary Yaou Sangaré, Niamey dénonce des manquements financiers et contractuels majeurs et accorde 45 jours à la CNPC, WAPCO et la SORAZ pour se conformer aux engagements bilatéraux et communautaires. L’heure des comptes a sonné dans le secteur pétrolier nigérien. Réuni pour évaluer la mise en œuvre des 45 engagements issus du protocole de partenariat signé le 18 mai 2026, le comité de suivi gouvernemental a rendu public ses conclusions particulièrement sévères à l’encontre des sociétés chinoises opérant sur la chaîne pétrolière nationale : la CNPC, WAPCO et la raffinerie de Zinder (SORAZ). Plus de 3 000 milliards de FCFA hors du circuit financier national Au cœur des griefs formulés par les autorités nigériennes figure la question cruciale du rapatriement des recettes d’exportation du brut. Depuis le lancement des exportations en avril 2024, plus de 3 000 milliards de FCFA de recettes n’ont toujours pas été rapatriés au Niger par la CNPC. Alors que l’État a intégralement remboursé au 30 mars 2026, le prêt commercial de 400 millions de dollars contracté en 2024, seuls 105 milliards de FCFA sont effectivement revenus dans les caisses nationales. Ce taux dérisoire d’environ 6% contre une moyenne communautaire supérieure à 70% au sein de l’UEMOA a privé le Trésor public de près de 17,4 milliards de FCFA de recettes directes et asséché les liquidités des banques locales. Sur le plan juridique, Niamey a tenu à rappeler la primauté absolue de la réglementation des changes de l’UEMOA sur les anciennes conventions dérogatoires datant de 2008 et 2019. L’État exige l’application immédiate du mécanisme pérenne négocié avec la BCEAO, avertissant qu’en cas de refus persistant, les sanctions de l’institut d’émission communautaire seront appliquées sans réserve. Sous-traitance locale et nigérisation : des engagements restés lettre morte Le réquisitoire gouvernemental met également en lumière des défaillances flagrantes en matière de contenu local et de gestion des ressources humaines : Contenu local opaque : Les quotas contractuels fixés pour 2026 (20% pour la CNPC, 25% pour WAPCO et 56% pour la SORAZ) ne sont appuyés par aucun justificatif probant. Les déclarations transmises comportent des doublons et des montants pluriannuels non ventilés, tandis que la SORAZ n’a fourni aucun état d’exécution. Remplacement des expatriés au point mort : Aucun plan de nigérisation sur quatre ans n’a été déposé par les trois entreprises. Le processus de recrutement local censé pourvoir 558 postes occupés par des expatriés sur les champs pétroliers d’Agadem n’a jamais été amorcé. Audits RH bloqués : La SORAZ et WAPCO refusent toujours d’engager l’audit indépendant de leurs effectifs. Réserves non certifiées : Depuis 2008, les volumes des réserves pétrolières du bloc d’Agadem reposent sur les seules déclarations unilatérales de la CNPC, sans aucune certification par un cabinet d’audit indépendant. Sur le plan énergétique interne, la SORAZ tourne actuellement à un régime réduit de 15 000 barils/jour (soit 75% de sa capacité nominale de 20 000 b/j), alimentant des tensions sur l’approvisionnement du marché domestique en carburant. Face à ce constat, le gouvernement nigérien a formellement notifié une mise en demeure assortie d’un délai d’exécution strict de 45 jours aux trois directions générales. Celles-ci doivent sans délai transmettre des états financiers rectifiés, déposer leurs plans de nigérisation, lancer les recrutements et coopérer pleinement à la certification indépendante des réserves d’Agadem. « Le partenariat avec la Chine est ancien et l’État entend le poursuivre, mais sur la base de la transparence, du respect strict des engagements et de la défense intransigeante des intérêts du Niger », a conclu le chef de la diplomatie nigérienne. À l’expiration du préavis, Niamey se réserve le droit de tirer toutes les conséquences juridiques, contractuelles et souveraines qui s’imposent. Avec les partenaires chinois, il faut nécessairement user du bâton et de la carotte. Ils sont des partenaires sans scrupules et prêts à tout pour uniquement leurs intérêts. En cette ère de refondation, l’état doit être ferme. C’est cela la souveraineté. items.title: Vinícius handed four-match ban, to miss Real Madrid’s Clasico against Barcelona
items.description: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Júnior has been handed a four-match suspension after pulling an opponent’s hair during his side’s 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday. The Brazilian was sent off in the 73rd minute after grabbing and tugging the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba as the two players sprinted down the pitch. Vinícius had scored moments earlier, but the goal was ruled out. The Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee announced the suspension shortly before Real Madrid’s Champions League match against Roma on Wednesday. According to the committee, Vinícius received a two-match ban for the hair-pulling incident and an additional two matches for his aggressive reaction to the referee after being shown the red card. Referee Isidro Díaz de Mera stated in his match report that the forward protested the decision by raising his voice and approaching him aggressively, adding that Vinícius had to be restrained by his teammates. The suspension means Vinícius will miss Real Madrid’s home fixture against Sevilla on Sunday and their trip to Barcelona the following week for the highly anticipated Clasico. He will also be unavailable for Madrid’s away matches against Racing Santander and Valencia. The four-match ban comes as a setback for Real Madrid, who will be without one of their key attacking players for several important domestic fixtures. items.title: Réfugiés sahraouis : à Genève, l’Algérie recadre sèchement le Maroc
items.description: L’Algérie a réitéré, mardi soir, son plaidoyer en faveur du maintien de l’aide et de la protection des réfugiés sahraouis , conformément aux obligations et aux engagements consacrés par la Convention de 1951 relative au statut des réfugiés. Dans une allocution prononcée à l’occasion de la 77e session du Comité exécutif du Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies pour les réfugiés (HCR), à Genève, le représentant permanent de l’Algérie, Idris Latreche, s’adressant au Haut-Commissaire, a estimé que l’attention portée aux réfugiés sahraouis ne devait toutefois pas occulter le processus politique visant à s’attaquer aux causes profondes de leur situation. « Comme vous l’avez souligné à juste titre, les engagements consacrés par cette convention doivent rester en vigueur. Ils doivent le rester parce que l’aide et la protection internationales ne relèvent pas de la charité, mais constituent des droits fondamentaux et intrinsèques des réfugiés, tant que les causes profondes des déplacements forcés qui les ont contraints à chercher refuge n’ont pas été traitées », a affirmé le diplomate algérien. Situation des réfugiés sahraouis : l’Algérie appelle à traiter les « causes profondes » « Cette analyse s’applique pleinement à la situation actuelle des réfugiés sahraouis. Si le regain d’intérêt pour leurs souffrances, à ce stade précis, est une évolution bienvenue, cette attention ne doit pas occulter le processus politique chargé de s’attaquer aux causes profondes de cette situation », a-t-il insisté. En tant que pays d’accueil des réfugiés sahraouis depuis plus de cinq décennies et principal contributeur financier à l’amélioration de leurs conditions de vie, l’Algérie appelle la communauté internationale à maintenir et à renforcer son soutien à ces populations contraintes de fuir leur territoire et la colonisation marocaine. Réfugiés sahraouis : les trois vérités de l’Algérie Toutefois, aux yeux d’Alger, toute initiative concernant cette question doit s’appuyer rigoureusement sur les « réalités » du terrain et, surtout, sur trois faits qu’elle considère comme incontestables. La première vérité concerne la spécificité de la situation des réfugiés sahraouis. « Ceux-ci ne sont pas des réfugiés ayant fui la précarité économique, des conditions climatiques extrêmes ou des guerres civiles internes, mais des personnes déplacées d’un territoire non autonome appelé Sahara occidental . Leur droit inaliénable à l’autodétermination demeure au cœur même de leur détresse », a souligné le représentant de l’Algérie. La deuxième vérité réside dans le fait que la volonté des réfugiés des camps sahraouis de Tindouf a toujours constitué, et constitue encore, le principe de référence auquel tous doivent se conformer, selon lui. « Les camps sont ouverts et se caractérisent par leur transparence. Ils accueillent de manière permanente plus de cinq entités des Nations Unies et plus de vingt organisations internationales non gouvernementales. Ils reçoivent également des visites régulières de donateurs internationaux, d’observateurs internationaux et de différents mécanismes des Nations Unies », a-t-il affirmé. Enfin, la troisième et dernière vérité assénée par le diplomate algérien concerne les principes fondamentaux de l’action humanitaire. « Même si cela peut sembler relever de l’évidence, je suis fermement convaincu de la nécessité de le rappeler encore et encore : l’aide humanitaire ne doit pas être instrumentalisée à des fins politiques ni servir d’outil de pression politique. La souffrance des réfugiés sahraouis ne doit pas non plus devenir une monnaie d’échange permettant de marquer des points politiques ou de poursuivre des objectifs étroits et égoïstes », a insisté M. Latrèche. On l’aura compris : il s’agit d’une réponse directe du représentant de l’Algérie à son homologue marocain, qui avait plutôt invité les bailleurs de fonds et les Nations Unies à réorienter l’aide humanitaire vers des solutions durables pour les populations des camps de Tindouf. Le représentant marocain préconise rien de moins que le rapatriement librement consenti, l’intégration locale ou la réinstallation, afin de mettre fin à un statu quo de plus de cinquante ans. « À la lumière de ces réalités fondamentales, cette délégation estime, avec une profonde conviction, qu’il faut éviter d’envoyer un message erroné au mauvais moment. Nous devons également éviter le risque de brouiller les distinctions entre les impératifs humanitaires et les réalités politiques », a estimé Idris Latrèche. « Enfin, nous devons nous abstenir de susciter toute confusion susceptible d’aggraver davantage les souffrances des réfugiés sahraouis, au lieu de leur apporter l’aide à laquelle ils ont pleinement droit », a-t-il complété. Réfugiés sahraouis : à Genève, Idris Latreche corrige la délégation marocaine Le diplomate algérien n’a pas manqué de critiquer vertement la position marocaine, estimant que la partie qu’il tient pour responsable de la situation au Sahara occidental ne saurait prétendre donner des leçons sur les solutions durables. « Il est profondément regrettable, voire surprenant, de voir la partie qui porte la responsabilité première et entière de cette situation tenter de donner des leçons à cet honorable comité sur les solutions durables. Passer du déni absolu à la prétention de détenir une autorité morale dont on se pose soi-même en garant… voilà ce que nous appelons de l’opportunisme dans sa pire expression. En réponse, je tiens à affirmer que la communauté internationale n’est pas aveugle aux faits et qu’elle n’ignore pas les racines de cette situation », a conclu Idris Latreche. L’article Réfugiés sahraouis : à Genève, l'Algérie recadre sèchement le Maroc est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.20 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.17
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · " style="width: 100%; min-height: 50px; max-height: 30000px; border: none; overflow: hidden; display: block;" scrolling="no"> The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.20 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.17 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.65 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 15 (Thursday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Omani FM meets PM Shehbaz, commends Pakistan's 'sustained diplomatic efforts' for regional peace
items.description: Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday and appreciated Pakistan’s “sustained diplomatic efforts” for de-escalation and peaceful solutions to regional challenges, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. Both Pakistan and Oman have been engaged in efforts for de-escalation after US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February resulted in a conflict that has now expanded further into the Middle East. Albusaidi’s meeting with PM Shehbaz was held on the second day of his two-day trip to Pakistan, during which he also attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) and held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. In his meeting with the Omani foreign minister, PM Shehbaz “highlighted that the strong bond of shared faith, geography, history, culture, and centuries of people-to-people exchanges between Pakistan and Oman provided a strong fraternal foundation to the bilateral relationship”, the PMO statement said. The premier underscored that Pakistan considered Oman a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region, it added. “The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the successful convening of the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission. “He hoped that the meeting would provide a strong foundation for further expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two brotherly countries,” the statement said. It further stated that PM Shehbaz “noted with deep satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on all regional and global issues”. He appreciated Oman’s “principled stance” of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes, the statement said. For his part, Albusaidi thanked the government of Pakistan for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation and “expressed satisfaction on successful holding of the 8th JMC session”, the PMO statement said. It added that the Omani foreign minister “agreed that it (JMC session) would pave the way for enhanced bilateral collaboration in diverse sectors for mutual benefit”. “The Omani foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s sustained diplomatic efforts towards de-escalating tensions and advancing peaceful solutions to regional challenges,” the statement read. It added that PM Shehbaz also witnessed the signing of the Protocol of the 8th session of the Pakistan-Oman JMC, as well as agreements and memoranda of understanding for bilateral cooperation between the two sides in the areas of media cooperation, news and information exchange, historical documentation and archives management, communication and information technology and facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges. ‘Totally unacceptable’ Earlier in the day, Albusaidi held a joint press conference with Deputy PM Dar, during which the latter said that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were “totally unacceptable”. At the outset of the press conference, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol relating to the commission. He said that this reflected “a shared resolve to further strengthen and expand bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. He said that the two sides would also sign an agreement for mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and official passports. “Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking,” he told the media. He added that the two ministers had also agreed to hold a business-to-business investment forum in Pakistan. The ministers discussed the situation in the Gulf as well, he said, adding that “Pakistan remained committed to contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”. Dar said that the two sides also exchanged views on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said that he conveyed Pakistan’s condemnation of the attacks. “I underscored that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable. My brother [Albusaidi] actually fully endorses this. Violations of international law pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said. “I reaffirmed Pakistan’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and our unwavering commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he said. They also “emphasised the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza”, Dar said. DPM Dar also stressed that India’s unilateral abeyance of the Indus Water Treaty was “a material breach of international law”. “This action threatens the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” Dar said. Speaking at the occasion, Albusaidi said the JMC had “provided an important opportunity to review the state of bilateral relations”. He said that two sides “reaffirmed the strength of the longstanding ties” between the two countries. “Both Oman and Pakistan attach great importance to dialogue and diplomacy as essential means of addressing regional challenges, easing tensions and promoting peace and stability,” Albusaidi said. He also appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic role in the US-Iran war . He reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further deepening our bilateral partnership and broadening cooperation across centres of mutual benefit”. The two countries agreed that dialogue and diplomacy were “the only way forward” to resolve regional conflicts, Dar said in response to a reporter’s question. “We are both on the same page,” he said. Meanwhile, Dar told reporters that a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would help expand business activities, adding that he was told that barring one, all countries had consented to the agreement. Responding to a question about the gaps in bilateral talks between the two countries, Dar said Albusaidi’s visit was previously delayed because Pakistan had been involved in mediation efforts between the US and Iran. Albusaidi added that discussions had continued “behind the scenes”. Responding to a question about the Strait of Hormuz, Albusaidi said that Oman was committed to “unhindered navigation” through the strait “because of its vitality to the global economy and the region”. JMC session The meeting of the commission was co-chaired by Dar and Albusaidi. The two sides “reaffirmed their close fraternal ties and commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, maritime and logistics connectivity, agriculture, industry, energy, workforce mobility, human resource development, education, IT, media and climate change, among other areas”, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Both ministers emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties, facilitating workforce mobility, and promoting exchanges of business delegations from both countries to unlock new opportunities for trade, investment and institutional collaboration. FM Dar stressed the need for “timely implementation of agreed outcomes through close institutional coordination and sustained engagement between joint working group meetings”, the statement added. According to FO, the Oman FM thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality, appreciated Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace and security, and reaffirmed Muscat’s commitment to further strengthening the longstanding partnership between the two countries. Dar commends Albusaidi’s efforts towards regional peace Speaking at the outset of the JMC session, Dar said the two had “worked out” certain areas of bilateral interest and discussed global issues in detail, including the US-Iran war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Gaza in their restricted meeting. Dar said the two sides had also discussed Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues. He commended Albusaidi’s leadership and efforts towards regional peace in the Middle East. “I personally greatly admire your efforts. I know how much hard work you have put in,” he said, noting that Pakistan’s position on the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was “very unique”. “We are members of both the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and, obviously, the United Nations and other multilateral bodies,” Dar said. He stressed, “There should not be any long gaps between bilateral engagements,” noting potential in the areas of trade, economic activities and investment opportunities. Dar said he had promised to visit Oman in 2027 to hold the next session of the commission there. He added that both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed possible meetings. He said Pakistan and Oman cooperated closely and cordially, adding that although their diplomatic relations had completed 55 years, their ties went back “centuries”. Dar said the two countries shared a history of “love and affection”, particularly in relation to Balochistan and Gwadar. Referring to discussions on Bab al-Mandab and recent developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Dar said both sides shared similar views on resolving regional issues. He said the impact of regional tensions was also visible in Pakistan, where energy supply chains had been affected, and fuel prices had skyrocketed, adding that the “common man could not afford the resulting burden.” Speaking on the occasion, Albusaidi said Oman was committed to further strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation in various fields that could bring greater benefits to the people of both countries. “I am delighted to be here with my delegation in Islamabad this morning, in this very warm, friendly and brotherly country, Pakistan, with which, as you have rightly said, we share bonds of history, culture, tradition and unity,” he said. He said the Pakistan-Oman JMC was one of the mechanisms for exploring further avenues of collaboration, adding that the two countries also had a business council and a political consultation mechanism between their foreign ministers. “We can do much more, and as we made a joint commitment this morning to make this meeting a success, I believe the more we do, the more we can deliver on the promise and the aspiration of our leaderships and our people,” Albusaidi said. He also commended Pakistan’s role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in the region. “Your efforts to encourage engagement, understanding, respect and recognition are commendable, and I salute you for all your efforts,” he said, adding that Oman greatly appreciated Pakistan’s role in providing space for dialogue between Iran and the US. Albusaidi said there was significant potential for economic cooperation between Oman and Pakistan, particularly in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy and food security. “The potential exists, and our task is to remove any obstacles and create the conditions that allow businesses to thrive so that we can fully benefit from this potential,” he said. He also called for greater cooperation in tourism, academic and technological fields, as well as more regular exchanges between the people of the two countries. “Once again, I appreciate the efforts of our private sector and industrial partners,” Albusaidi said, adding that he looked forward to further discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation. According to a joint statement, the two sides agreed to hold the ninth session of the JMC next year. After the session concluded, Albusaidi posted on that he had a “constructive day” in Islamabad co-chairing JMC session with Dar. “We reviewed practical ways to deepen our longstanding partnership in trade, investment, energy, logistics and other priority areas, and agreed on closer follow-up to turn opportunities into results,” he said, expressing gratitude for the “warm hospitality and the shared commitment to cooperation and regional dialogue”. Dar, Omani FM call for sustained bilateral engagement Earlier in the day, Dar also held a bilateral meeting with Albusaidi ahead of the JMC session, FO said. The visiting dignitary had arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday on a two-day visit. The two ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal ties between Pakistan and Oman and underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade, investment and people-to-people contacts, according to FO. “The two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in advancing lasting peace and stability,” FO said. Albusaidi commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and security, while Dar acknowledged and appreciated Oman’s constructive role and shared aspirations for regional peace and stability, the statement added. A day earlier, FO said the JMC session would review the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Oman bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation. The visit “reflects the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and is expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation”.

items.title: Pakistani, Chinese armies begin joint training exercise in Xinjiang
items.description: GILGIT: A joint training exercise of Pakistani and Chinese armies, “Karakoram 2026”, began in the Xinjiang province of China on Wednesday. The opening ceremony of Karakoram 2026 was held at a training base in Korla city, according to the China Military Bugle, the official media account of Beijing’s armed forces. The two sides exchanged counter-terrorism experience and Pakistani troops observed some Chinese weapons and equipment. Before the drill commenced, Colonel Chen Xi, the press secretary of China’s defence ministry, said last week that the exercise would help the two sides deepen exchanges and cooperation and enhance their ability to jointly respond to the threat of terrorism. He said the training would focus on “joint anti-terrorism clearance operations at high altitudes”. The press secretary added that the drills would involve drone operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and would cover “joint command and live-force exercises”, according to China’s Xinhua news agency. Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership. In September, the two countries held a joint patrolling exercise at Mantika Pass, at an altitude of approximately 4,700 metres, near Khunjerab top situated in the upper area of GB’s Hunza. In May, they reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral military cooperation and strategic coordination. Additional input from Anadolu Agency

items.title: Pope out of bed, progress ‘normal’ after cancer operation
items.description: Pope Leo XIV is out of bed, walking and eating after doctors removed a cancerous tumour from his lung, while post-surgery tests show his progress is “normal”, his doctors said Wednesday. Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in Tuesday’s operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is now awaiting the results of a biopsy to determine if the cancer has spread. Blood tests and a chest X-ray meanwhile “confirm a normal post-operative course”, doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora said in a statement released by the Vatican. “The values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed,” they said. The discovery on Tuesday that a nodule detected in Leo’s lung was cancerous has plunged the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty. “It’s a shock for everyone. We’re in ‘wait-and-see’ mode,” a Vatican source told AFP. Doctors said his recovery was “proceeding as expected” and the pontiff had eaten both breakfast and lunch, been walking about his room, and had done some respiratory physiotherapy. Another Vatican source said the pope had even celebrated a mass on Wednesday in a specially prepared room on the 10th floor of the hospital, where is staying. The papal suite on the same floor is where popes are usually treated. It has a private chapel but is currently being refurbished. – ‘Show my spiritual support’ – The sporty 71-year-old, elected as the first pope from the United States only last year, made the surprise announcement that he would be undergoing surgery after Sunday prayers. Messages of support flooded in from around the world, including from Britain’s King Charles III, who is also being treated for an undisclosed cancer. A banner flying outside the hospital read “Long live the pope!” and a handful of people recited prayers for the hospitalised pontiff. Nearby, nun Angele Bilegue said she had come to pray for Leo. “I’m not worried. I came to express my closeness, to show my spiritual support, because I also came for Pope Francis,” she told AFP. Leo’s predecessor, the Argentine Francis, spent five weeks last year being treated for double pneumonia at the same hospital, before his death at the Vatican on April 21, 2025. Experts said much would depend on how advanced Leo’s cancer was, and whether it had spread, but the Vatican has said it had been detected early and was localised. Before the operation, the Vatican said the pope’s recovery should take around a week. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20. “If we are dealing with stage I or II disease, and recovery is good… the patient can resume a normal life and usual activities within a few weeks,” Alain Gelibter, an oncologist at Rome’s Policlinico Umberto I hospital, told AFP. The Chicago-born Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving on Tuesday. In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope’s health during the operation. – New uncertainty – The shock news of the tennis-playing pope’s illness has rattled the Catholic Church. Expert Marco Politi, who has spent decades covering the Vatican, told AFP: “The Church is now in a state of uncertainty. When Leo was elected everyone foresaw a long papacy.” Hendro Munsterman, a theologian and expert for Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad, told AFP “we have a pope whom everyone described as young, active and athletic. Now, we have a pope who also has his own vulnerabilities, which will change his image.” His health issues may prompt him to speed up personnel appointments, Munsterman said. Politi said Leo had been working on “repairing” rifts between various wings of the Church, and many will want him “to continue with this important mission as soon as possible”. Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, newly nominated to the influential role of dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrated mass on St Peter’s Square on Wednesday instead of Leo. The surgery has raised questions about whether Leo will go ahead with a lengthy visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he worked as a missionary for two decades. items.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK 6-3 in Champions League
items.description: Bradley Barcola silenced his critics as the Liverpool forward ended his goal drought with a hat-trick in a chaotic 6-3 win against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday. Barcola had come under fire for some lacklustre performances since his blockbuster £123 million ($161 million) move from Paris Saint-Germain in August. But the France forward finally started to live up to his hefty price tag with his first goals for Liverpool in his seventh appearance. Barcola struck twice before the interval at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the first half with his maiden goal for the club. Jeremie Frimpong netted the fourth after the break against the Austrian champions before Barcola completed his treble. There was still time for Lewis Koumas to score his first Champions League goal as Liverpool maintained their 100 percent record in this season’s tournament after beating Atletico Madrid in their opening game. It was a welcome boost for Iraola following his first defeat in eight games as Liverpool manager when Premier League leaders Manchester City won 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday. Iraola this week said he has “100 per cent” trust in Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who has struggled mightily since joining from Bayer Leverkusen last year. Injuries to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, who all missed the trip to Austria, increased the pressure on Wirtz and Barcola to carry the Liverpool attack. The pair repaid Iraola’s faith with a much-needed display of their undoubted qualities. Now Iraola will demand they produce that level of intensity and quality on a regular basis. The trip to Linz was the second of six games in 18 days for Liverpool, forcing Iraola to make changes in a bid to save his players from burnout. Reds captain Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz were all rested as Frimpong, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha came in. – Clinical Barcola – After some disjointed displays at the start of Iraola’s reign, this was an indication of what they can become under the former Bournemouth boss, although he will still be concerned about their defensive issues. Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the 22nd minute, rising highest to meet Tsimikas’s corner with a thumping header past LASK keeper Lukas Jungwirth. The on-loan Barcelona defender’s goal was swiftly followed by one for Barcola 96 seconds later. Ngumoha was the catalyst with an incisive run into the LASK area and Barcola applied the finishing touch as he guided a clinical finish beyond Jungwirth. Iraola’s men were running riot and Barcola scored their third in the 37th minute. It was a riposte to the criticism of Wirtz and Barcola as the pair combined to cut through the LASK defence. Barcola picked out Wirtz and the German played a pinpoint return pass that allowed the 24-year-old to fire past Jungwirth. Frimpong has also frustrated Liverpool fans since signing last year, making his goal in the 51st minute a welcome tonic for the Dutch right-back. Tsimikas got to the byline and lofted a cross towards Frimpong, who belied his diminutive stature with a towering header into the bottom corner. Robert Ljubicic reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute with a composed finish from Yvan Dibango’s pass. But Barcola sealed his treble with a nimble finish from Frimpong’s pass in the 66th minute. Teed up by Frimpong, Koumas hit Liverpool’s sixth with a searing strike in the 72nd minute. Despite the introduction of Van Dijk and fellow defender Joe Gomez, Liverpool lost control in the closing stages. Florian Flecker’s diving header two minutes later punished slack Liverpool defending. Flecker struck again with a close-range finish in the 77th minute, but nothing could spoil Barcola’s big night. items.title: Man United line up three-man shortlist as sack looms for Michael Carrick
items.description: Manchester United are reportedly considering Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for Michael Carrick if the club decides to part ways with its current manager. According to talkSPORT, the three managers have attracted interest from different figures within the Old Trafford hierarchy as pressure mounts on Carrick following a difficult run of results. United’s reported interest comes after their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, which extended their winless run to five matches across all competitions. The result also followed a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur, a run of form that has raised concerns about the team’s performances and Carrick’s tactical decisions. The defeat to Atletico also prompted defender Lisandro Martinez to criticise technical director Jason Wilcox over what he reportedly viewed as insufficient squad strengthening. United will look to end their poor run when they face historic rivals Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday. Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, the station’s chief live football anchor, Adrian Durham, suggested Carrick’s position could become increasingly difficult if the team fails to improve. “Does it feel like an inevitability? Absolutely, that Michael Carrick will go,” Durham said. He added that Carrick would need to turn around the team’s results to improve his chances of remaining in the job. Durham also expressed concerns about Carrick’s tactical decisions in the Atletico Madrid match, arguing that some of the changes made during the game contributed to United’s defeat. Among the three reported candidates, Nagelsmann and Conte are said to be available for an immediate appointment. Conte left Napoli by mutual consent in May, while Nagelsmann reportedly departed his position as Germany coach following the country’s elimination by Paraguay in the round of 32 at the World Cup. The report said United’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, was advocating for Nagelsmann internally as a potential successor should the club decide to dismiss Carrick. Hurzeler, meanwhile, remains under contract with Brighton until 2029 after signing an extension in May. The German coach is reportedly favoured by Wilcox and has overseen a strong start to the Premier League season, with Brighton winning four of their opening six matches to sit third in the standings. Hurzeler has also guided Brighton to victory over Manchester United in the third round of the EFL Cup in September, adding to his credentials as a potential candidate. However, Manchester United have not been reported to have made a formal appointment decision, and Carrick’s immediate future could depend on the team’s results in the coming matches. items.title: You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar over what he described as disrespectful comments about President Bola Tinubu, saying anyone seeking the presidency must show discipline and respect for public institutions. Shettima spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election. In his remarks, Shettima said Atiku’s repeated presidential bids and recent policy proposals did not, in his view, excuse language he considered disrespectful toward the sitting president. He also questioned how Atiku’s proposed production subsidies would be funded. “Those who want equity must come with clean hands. You can call him Bola. If you like, you can call him Adekunle. But the truth is that he is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Atiku Abubakar. I will still respect him and call him his former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar. “I will not follow suit with the maverick Babachir Lawal and call him Kachalla, no. But believe me, Atiku Abubakar, who has contested for the presidency of this country for the eighth time, is no Abraham Lincoln. He is more of Oginga Odinga.” Shettima framed his criticism as an argument about the conduct expected of presidential contenders, saying the higher the office sought, the greater the responsibility candidates bear in their words and dealings with public institutions. “The presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is not an ordinary political prize. It is the highest expression of constitutional authority in our country. And those who aspire to occupy it must demonstrate, even before they get there, the qualities they will expect of themselves, if entrusted with the responsibility of leading more than 200 million Nigerians. “Political ambition is not merely the desire to occupy public office. It is a test of character, cerebral strength, intellectual maturity, and responsibility. The higher the office a person seeks, the greater the discipline expected in his words, conduct, and relationship with public institutions,” he added. Turning to Atiku’s proposal on production subsidies, Shettima questioned the cost and the competing priorities that might be affected. “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, this political season has become a masterclass in cinematic comedy. Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal for production subsidies raises questions that some changes cannot answer. Who pays? Who benefits? And which competing priorities must surrender their funding? A change in ideological wardrobe cannot balance a national budget.” The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council inauguration, held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja, formally brought the expanded campaign structure into focus as the ruling party prepared for the 2027 general election. The post You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .
